title: Types & primary keys
summary: Add lab_products with typed columns and a clear primary key.
description:
Add lab_products with typed columns and a clear primary key.

Why: Types and primary keys are the anchors every FK will reference. Get PKs wrong and later relationship tasks cannot attach constraints.
objectives: Create lab_products with id PK, sku, price, in_stock
hints: Read gate errors as cause→effect: each message names what Postgres still lacks.
starterCodePrisma:
model LabProduct {
  id      Int     @id @default(autoincrement())
  sku     String  @unique
  price   Decimal @db.Decimal(10, 2)
  inStock Boolean @default(true) @map("in_stock")
  @@map("lab_products")
}
why: Types and primary keys are the anchors every FK will reference. Get PKs wrong and later relationship tasks cannot attach constraints.
pitfalls: Column exists but is not marked PK.
Using a non-integer id when the task expects SERIAL/Int @id.
teachAlong: Next tasks will REFERENCE this id.
mappingNotes: Compare your ORM/schema code with the Equivalent SQL panel. The task gate introspects Postgres — only real tables/FKs count.
